analysis:
Examined the head text of ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift (lines 488-1450) and the ClusterService.swift patch. The only functional changes are in the update-handling path. ClusterOnboardingUpdate.oneBuild (new, near line 448) returns true only when every pinned member answered with a non-nil runtime digest and all digests are equal. In ClusterService (patch hunk around 971-984), after the changed-set is computed, the service now waits when the Macs run different builds or a member has not answered. It does not re-plan until both agree, and it logs the wait line once, deduplicated through the lock-guarded updateWaitLine. It also adds pairUpdate progress reading in the status publish path (line 943) via ClusterPairUpdate.readProgress from the service directory.

Security view: the change is more conservative (fail-closed, wait) and removes no checks. The digests come from peerFacts.runtimeBinarySHA256 on an already-established, authenticated link, and the local digest comes from the local process. No new network surface, key handling, or coordinator authorization change appears. The waiting state creates no bypass: re-planning still requires the control command lock and the existing flow. A peer that lies about its digest could keep the leader in a waiting state, but that is the same trust level as before and only affects availability, with no new privilege. The onboarding flow text (menu, chooseAndServe, provision, register) is context in the unchanged region and the changed ranges don't touch it. Unverified: the content and permissions of the update progress file read by ClusterPairUpdate.readProgress (not supplied) and its parsing robustness. Also unseen are the truncated tail of the patch and the exact semantics of `pinned` when a member id is absent from `current`. A low-confidence integration question remains, so a deeper look at readProgress file trust is warranted, but no concrete regression is evidenced.
